{{Short description|None}}
{{Use Canadian English|date=March 2026}}
{{Monarchy of Canada sidebar}}

The following is a list of the governors and governors general of Canada. Though the present-day office of the [[Governor General of Canada]] is legislatively covered under the ''[[Constitution Act, 1867]]'' and legally constituted by the ''[[Letters Patent, 1947]]'', the institution is, along with the institution of the Crown it represents, the oldest continuous and uniquely Canadian institution in Canada, having existed in an unbroken line since the appointment of [[Samuel de Champlain]] in 1627.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/pch/documents/services/royal-symbols-titles/crnMpls-eng.pdf |title=A Crown of Maples: Constitutional Monarchy in Canada |last=Department of Canadian Heritage |publisher=Queen's Printer for Canada |year=2015 |isbn=978-1-100-20079-8 |location=Ottawa |page=34 }}</ref>

==Governors of the Province of Quebec, 1760–1786==
Following the [[Seven Years' War]], control passed from France to Great Britain in the terms of the [[Treaty of Paris (1763)|Treaty of Paris]], creating the British [[Province of Quebec (1763–1791)|Province of Quebec]]. Governors subsequently served under the [[Monarchy of the United Kingdom|British monarchy]].

== Administrators ==
{{Main|Administrator of the Government of Canada}}
[[File:Lyman Poore Duff.jpg|thumb|[[Chief Justice of Canada|Chief Justice]] [[Lyman Duff]] was administrator of Canada in 1940.]]
The following is a list of [[Administrator of the Government of Canada|Administrators of the Government]], Justices of the [[Supreme Court of Canada]] who were acting governors appointed as the result of the death, resignation, prolonged absence of the sitting viceroy, or for any other reason:

# [[Chief Justice of Canada|Chief Justice]] Sir [[Lyman Duff]], between the death of Lord Tweedsmuir and the arrival of Lord Athlone (February 11 to June 21, 1940);<ref>{{cite journal|last=Gosse |first=Richard |title=The Four Courts of Sir Lyman Duff |journal=The Canadian Bar Review |volume=53 |number=3 |date=1 September 1975 |pages=511–512}}</ref>
# Senior Puisne Justice [[Patrick Kerwin]], during the absence of Governor General Lord Alexander and Chief Justice [[Thibaudeau Rinfret]] (June 11 to August 2, 1951).<ref>{{cite book |first=Stephen |last=McKenna |title=Grace and Wisdom: Patrick G. Kerwin, Chief Justice of Canada |publisher=Petra Books |date=2020 | page=101 |isbn=978-1-927032-68-8}}</ref>
# Chief Justice Thibaudeau Rinfret, from the departure of the Lord Alexander to the installation of Vincent Massey (January 28 to February 28, 1952);
# Chief Justice [[Robert Taschereau]], from the death of Georges Vanier to the installation of Roland Michener (March 5 to April 17, 1967);<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2021/01/21/gov-gen-julie-payette-has-resigned-what-happens-now.html |title=Gov. Gen. Julie Payette has resigned. What happens now? |work=[[The Toronto Star]] |first=Jacques |last=Gallant |date=21 January 2021 |access-date=18 February 2021}}</ref>
# Chief Justice [[Bora Laskin]], while Governor General Jules Léger was recovering from a stroke (July 2 to December 9, 1974);<ref>{{cite book |first=Philip |last=Girard |title=Bora Laskin: Bringing Law to Life |publisher=University of Toronto Press |date=2015 | page=423 |isbn=978-1-4426-1688-2}}</ref>
# Chief Justice [[Beverley McLachlin]], while Governor General Adrienne Clarkson was hospitalized (July 8 to July 11, 2005);.<ref name="Silver">{{Cite web |last=Silver |first=Janet E. |date=2021-01-22 |title=Orders-in-council and royal assents not affected by GG's resignation |url=https://ipolitics.ca/2021/01/22/orders-in-council-and-royal-assents-not-affected-by-ggs-resignation/ |url-status=live |access-date=2021-02-17|website=iPolitics|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122231836/https://ipolitics.ca/2021/01/22/orders-in-council-and-royal-assents-not-affected-by-ggs-resignation/ |archive-date=2021-01-22 }}</ref>
# Chief Justice [[Richard Wagner (judge)|Richard Wagner]], from the resignation of Julie Payette to the installation of Mary Simon (January 22 to July 26, 2021).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/canadas-top-judge-is-now-acting-governor-general-but-expert-urges-speedy-replacement/ |title=Canada's top judge is now acting Governor General, but expert urges speedy replacement |publisher=[[CTV News]] |first=Graham |last=Slaughter |date=22 January 2021 |access-date=18 February 2021}}</ref>
